summary:
[`samples/hello-plugin`](../samples/hello-plugin/src/lib.rs) is a small
plugin to start from.

title: The plugin
summary:
A plugin is a type implementing [`Plugin`]: a manifest and a `register`
function.

title: Reading and changing: `Env` and commands
summary: Plugins never change the kernel's state directly.

title: Screens
summary: A screen implements [`Screen`].

title: Settings
summary:
A setting is a constant with its id and the type of its value
(`Setting<bool>`, `Setting<i64>` or `Setting<Text>` for choices,
languages, lists and text).

summary:
Plugins are tested with the real kernel and an in-memory storage, as the
sample's [test](../samples/hello-plugin/tests/hello.rs) does.

plugin the way its users will meet it, before it is published.

summary:
A plugin that works with books never names the reader plugin: it uses
what `builtin` defines for every reader, so a reader of one's own (bound

around it go on work

summary: A plugin can offer others more than the kernel knows of.

summary:
A page layer (`layers::PageLayerSpec`) draws on every page a reader
shows: side notes, a reading ruler, change bars.

title: Widgets with settings
summary: A widget may have settings of its own, such as where its text sits.

summary:
A preset is a ready-made set of setting values chosen as a whole

title: Passwords and keys
summary:
Plugins keep passwords, API keys and tokens with
`Command::set_secret(SecretChange::keep(id, label, value))` and read them
with `env.secrets().get(id)`.

summary:

title: Screens that run in real time
summary:

summary: PaperPaw's code guidelines ([CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md#code-guidelines)) hold for plugins too: length limits, errors on user data, memory, comments.
